summary: This Mining Technology article, dated September 9, 2021, lists the five largest iron ore mines in Indonesia by 2020 production, based on GlobalData's mining database. The mines are the Yiwan Mine, Gag Island Project, Pomalaa Mine, Pakal Island Mine and Nalo Baru Mine, each with its location, owner and estimated 2020 output in million tonnes per annum (MTPA). Most of the page is navigation, forms and promotional boilerplate, which was ignored.
one_line: Ranks Indonesia's five largest iron ore mines by estimated 2020 production using GlobalData's mining database.
key_facts: The article is titled 'Five largest iron ore mines in Indonesia in 2020' and is dated September 9, 2021.
The list ranks Indonesia's largest iron ore mines by production according to GlobalData's mining database.
The Yiwan Mine is located in South Kalimantan and is owned by Yiwan Mining.
The Yiwan Mine produced an estimated 2.547 MTPA of iron ore in 2020.
The Gag Island Project is located in West Papua and is owned by Indonesia Asahan Aluminium.
The Gag Island Project is a surface mine that produced an estimated 1.06 MTPA of iron ore in 2020 and will operate until 2047.
The Pomalaa Mine is located in South East Sulawesi and is owned by Indonesia Asahan Aluminium.
The Pomalaa Mine produced an estimated 0.943 MTPA of iron ore in 2020.
The Pakal Island Mine is a surface mine located in North Maluku and is owned by Indonesia Asahan Aluminium.
The Pakal Island Mine produced an estimated 0.515 MTPA of iron ore in 2020.
The Nalo Baru Mine is a surface mine located in Jambi and is owned by Earthstone Holdings.
The Nalo Baru Mine produced an estimated 0.027 MTPA of iron ore in 2020 and will operate until 2031.
The GlobalData mines and projects database tracks all operating and developing mines and projects globally.
GlobalData provides business information to 4,000 of the world's largest companies, according to the article.
